question: access

request.from: a cloud container in a datacenter network, one IP
request.body: an MCP initialize request (jsonrpc 2.0, protocolVersion 2025-06-18, clientInfo public-agents-researcher 1.0), Content-Type application/json, Accept application/json and text/event-stream

headers.www-authenticate: Bearer realm="OAuth", resource_metadata="https://mcp.linear.app/.well-known/oauth-protected-resource/mcp", error="invalid_token", error_description="Missing or invalid access token"

decoded.protected-resource-metadata: 200; resource https://mcp.linear.app/mcp; authorization_servers: https://mcp.linear.app (the MCP host is its own authorization server); scopes_supported: read, write; bearer_methods_supported: header
decoded.authorization-server-metadata: 200 at https://mcp.linear.app/.well-known/oauth-authorization-server; registration_endpoint present (/register); scopes_supported read, write, openid, email; PKCE S256; grants authorization_code, refresh_token, jwt-bearer; token auth client_secret_basic, client_secret_post, none; authorization_grant_profiles_supported id-jag; client_id_metadata_document_supported true
decoded.rest: GET https://api.linear.app/graphql with no Authorization header and no Content-Type answers 400, a CSRF refusal asking for a content-type or an x-apollo-operation-name header; the request is refused before authentication is considered, so this run says nothing about the GraphQL API's keyless answer

finding: With no credentials, an MCP initialize POST to mcp.linear.app/mcp answers 401 with a full Bearer challenge (realm OAuth, the protected-resource metadata URL, error invalid_token, a description) and the same error as a JSON body. The metadata names mcp.linear.app as its own authorization server with two scopes, read and write. That server advertises dynamic registration, public clients (auth method none), PKCE S256, the jwt-bearer grant with the id-jag grant profile, and client-id metadata documents. The one REST surface Linear documents is GraphQL, and a bare keyless GET on it answers 400 as a potential cross-site request forgery, before any authentication check, so the REST column of this probe is empty rather than 401. Same challenge shape as the 2026-09-11 measurement in the entry's notes. Nothing here measures what the server does with a credential.
